top_ai_signals.name: Thermal Noise & Sensor Consistency
top_ai_signals.summary: The sensor noise test found that 100% of this image is perfectly smooth - a physical impossibility for any real camera.
top_ai_signals.what_found: 100% of pixel blocks have near-zero internal variance, meaning they're completely flat at the sub-pixel level. Real cameras always produce baseline photon noise everywhere, even in blurry areas - this image doesn't. Spatial energy (0.00) is also atypically low, confirming the transitions are unnaturally smooth throughout.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: This specific combination - widespread flatness plus low spatial energy - is a documented fingerprint of diffusion-model generation, because AI samples from a mathematically smooth distribution rather than capturing real-world photon chaos.
top_ai_signals.caveat: Heavy compression, denoising, upscaling, or added grain filters can all change the noise profile independently of whether the image was generated or photographed.

This balanced exposure is realistic-looking but not diagnostic - it fits equally well for a careful real photograph and a modern AI generator.
top_inconclusive_signals.why_it_matters: Lighting is most useful when it's either suspiciously perfect (AI) or clearly clipping (real). A balanced middle-ground doesn't give us enough to work with, so this signal defers to others.
top_inconclusive_signals.caveat: HDR post-processing, tone mapping, strong flash, and professional retouching can all alter exposure profiles - introducing 'AI-like' qualities into real photos or vice versa.
